stories.title: Seabird Sees Miracle Recovery After Avian Flu Wiped Them Out
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Three years ago, avian flu completely wiped out a colony of sandwich terns on England's south coast, leaving zero birds behind. Thanks to years of dedicated conservation work, those terns have come back and multiplied to 756 birds today. Even better, little terns, ringed plovers, and other seabirds have moved in alongside them. It's a real comeback story, built by people who refused to give up on a damaged habitat. Nature, given a chance, found its way back.
stories.why_good: A wildlife population that was completely destroyed has fully recovered and grown thanks to real, completed conservation efforts, with no ongoing suffering at the center of the story.

stories.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
stories.label: people
stories.summary: On 230 acres of Montana wilderness, a guest ranch called Erik's Ranch & Retreats has built its whole operation around giving autistic adults real, meaningful jobs. The staff work as wranglers, cooks, guides, and concierges, running the ranch for visiting guests just like any other resort. It's a place built on the idea that people with autism don't need to be sidelined from the workforce, they need the right environment to thrive in it. Their own motto says it best: sheets, towels, and lives changed daily. It's a beautiful example of a workplace designed around people, not the other way around.
stories.why_good: It's a real, operating program that has already changed how autistic adults are employed and valued, not a proposal or a study.
